text:
Maya: Heads up — noticed a ~2.5x spike in SSE early-close events around 2026-03-21T22:03Z. Console traces show rapid route 'slab' swaps during the rollout window. Anyone else seeing reconnect churn? :eyes:

jonathan: Yup, seeing it in eu-west. WS clients show a reconnect loop, two resume attempts inside ~150ms. Looks like the routing decision returned a different slab_id mid-session so the client gave up and reconnected.

Lena: I have logs that look like sticky-lease TTL didn't make it to the edge proxy during the slab flip. We'll need to confirm which component nuked affinity.

Maya: Sharing a quick log snippet (sanitized) — note handoff_reason is empty, which makes it hard to filter these in the console:

```
2026-03-21T22:03:12.341Z route=route-42 slab_id=slab-7 session_id=abc123 conn_close=early reason="" client_ip=1.2.3.4
2026-03-21T22:03:12.492Z route=route-83 slab_id=slab-12 resume_attempt=1
```

ara: My rollback job for slab-rollout toggled `drain=true` but didn't wait for conn_count=0. That will cause active sockets to be steered to another slab — some client libs then fail resume and trigger fresh sessions.

Sam: That matches billing spikes we saw: reconnect counted as new session and caused duplicate metering for ~4k short-lived reconnects. We need a dedupe heuristic in metering or a short grace window.

devex-bot: deploy: rolled slab-rollout-canary down to 10% at 2026-03-21T22:12Z per safety triggers.

Lena: Proposal: when slab_rollout=true, emit a specific metric `slab_handoff_reason=drain` and set `handoff_hint=delayed` on active-connections so console can show "planned handoff" vs "unexpected". That will let ops filter rollout noise.

jonathan: Also add tags `slab_id` and `route_version` to reconnect events so we can build the panel that correlates reconnects -> slab swaps. For the reconnect itself, add a `same_resume_within_ms` field when applicable.

Maya: @ara can you add a lightweight proxy header `X-Slab-Handoff: delayed` when we mark a slab draining? If proxies emit it into logs we can add immediate parsers to the console.

ara: I can. Small PR to proxy to set the header when slab-drain flag is set, plus a log line `slab_handoff=drain delayed=true`. But we also need an SRE runbook entry: how to pause rollout and reduce canary percent if reconnect rate > threshold.

Sam: For billing: implement an opt-in grace window (default 500ms) where reconnections by same client_id + resume_id are not billed as new sessions. We can gate this behind account flag to avoid changing global semantics immediately.

Lena: I'll add the metric and create a console panel: `slab_handoff_delta` that splits by `slab_id` and `route_version`. We should also plot `conn_close=early` against `drain=true` events.

Maya: Action list: 1) @ara push proxy header + log PR, 2) @Lena add metric + dashboard panel, 3) @Sam prototype meter dedupe grace-window, 4) DevEx add rollout flag `slab_rollout_canary` and update rollout playbook. I'll coordinate cross-team comms. :thumbsup:

jonathan: One more UX ask — when console shows a spike we should surface the active rollout config (canary pct, drain=true slab list) in the alert so oncall knows it might be rollout-induced.

ara: Agreed. I'll include rollout metadata in the proxy logs and make sure the change is backwards compatible. PR in ~30m.

Sam: I'll start a small load test to reproduce the reconnect behavior and validate the 500ms dedupe threshold.

Maya: Thanks all. If anyone hits immediate churn channel me and I'll flip the canary to 0%.
